newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech April real ind output rises 6.3 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech April real ind output rises 6.3 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Czech real industrial output in April rose 6.3 percent, year-on-year, putting real output for the first four months of the year down 0.1 percent year-on-year, the statistical bureau (CSU) said on Monday.
It added that average industrial monthly wages grew, in nominal terms, 14.7 percent, year-on-year, in April, after 14.6 percent growth in March.
The CSU also said that real construction output for April grew by 5.9 percent, year-on-year, after 2.0 percent year-on-year growth in March.
The CSU said industrial sales for April, in real terms, rose by 9.9 percent, year-on-year.
NOTE. The average nominal industrial wage in April was 10,357 crowns compared with 9,844 in March.

In January, the CSU changed its methodology for calculating industrial production. The new methodology excludes multiple calculation of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials and commodities, which were included in output data at every stage under the old method measuring the gross value of all goods produced.
The new index measures output changes by units, weight or other measurements, of the total of 1,304 products out of 879 product groups consisting of one or more similar products.

The product groups's output indices are placed in sectors, using weighting equal to their weight in the respective sector. The overall index is calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
